name: Conversational Action Pill Triage & Optical Depth-of-Field Layering
description: Hero section interaction architecture combining intentional optical blur (filter: blur(4px)) on ambient intro text, cadence-gated typewriter storytelling with stepped cursor, and a responsive triage cluster of action pill buttons with one-click clipboard copy.
designPhilosophy: Treating hero landing pages as conversational triage stations rather than passive promotional billboards. Leverages intentional optical blur (filter: blur(4px)) on secondary intro metadata to simulate camera lens depth-of-field, paired with typewriter conversational cadence and immediate interactive response pill buttons.
appropriateUseCases: Creative studio and boutique agency intake heroes
AI agent interaction platforms and concierge onboarding
Freelance consultant and bespoke service intake portals
implementationApproach: 1. Ambient Optical Depth of Field: Intro text uses filter: blur(4px), pointer-events: none, select-none to establish an unfocused ambient camera layer in the background. 2. Cadence-Gated Typewriter: Custom hook reveals characters at 38ms intervals following an initial 600ms contemplation delay, rendered with a stepped 1s blinking cursor that vanishes upon completion. 3. Action Pill Triage Grid: Responsive cluster of high-contrast pill buttons (bg-white text-black, rounded-full, text-14px) offering immediate conversation avenues. 4. One-Click Clipboard Telemetry: Outline pill featuring inline SVG icon and navigator.clipboard.writeText integration with instant tooltip confirmation. 5. Independent Entrance Timing: Action pills slide up 400ms after load without blocking on typewriter text completion.
performanceConsiderations: Blur filter is applied strictly to static, non-composited text elements without active animation, ensuring zero GPU overdraw penalties.
accessibilityRequirements: Intro blurred text retains full DOM accessibility and aria-hidden='false' for screen readers. Clipboard copy action announces 'Email copied to clipboard' via an aria-live region. All action pills support standard Tab and Enter keyboard activation.
